# SHERATAN

> A frontend framework with one legal way to structure an app. Signals and
> tagged templates, no virtual DOM, no bundler. A checker enforces the module
> rules and reports every violation as JSON with a code and a fix.
> This is llms.txt v0: it covers what the runtime ships today.

## 1. The trap — read this first

A template hole is reactive only when it receives the signal itself.
JavaScript evaluates `${…}` before `html` runs, so a *call* inside a hole
hands the runtime a plain value that never updates.

```ts
html`<span>${s.total}</span>`          // ✓ updates
html`<span>${s.total()}</span>`        // ✗ read once at mount (SHR-V003)
html`<span>${s.total() * 2}</span>`    // ✗ read once; make a computed
const t = s.total(); html`${t}`        // ✗ read once, same reason
```

This looks like every other framework and is wrong here. Any expression — maths,
formatting, a ternary choosing markup — becomes a named `computed`, and the
hole gets the computed.

## 2. API

```ts
import { signal, computed, watch, batch, resource, mutation, stream, onDispose, flush, html, each, render } from 'sheratan';
```

<!-- generated from TSDoc by packages/core/scripts/llms.ts -->

| API | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `signal<T>(initial: T): Signal<T>` | A writable value. Read it by calling it, write it with `.set()`. Writing an equal value (`Object.is`) notifies nobody, and the value is frozen, so state can only be replaced, never mutated (SPEC §5 Immutability). |
| `computed<T>(fn: () => T): Accessor<DeepReadonly<T>>` | A derived value: evaluated on first read, cached until a source changes. Every expression over state is a named computed — that is the one way to derive (SPEC §9 "Holes take signals by reference"). |
| `watch(fn: () => void): Disposer` | Runs `fn` now, and again whenever something it read changes. Returns the disposer; the owning module disposes it automatically (SPEC §5b). |
| `batch<T>(fn: () => T): T` | Writes inside `fn` commit once, when the outermost batch ends. |
| `resource<T, K extends readonly unknown[]>(options: ResourceOptions<T, K>): Resource<T>` | Async state on a reactive key. The request is aborted when the key changes, when `abort()` is called and when the owning module unmounts; an identical key is not refetched, a superseded response is discarded, and errors are values. Legal in `*.effects.ts` only (`SHR-L004`). |
| `mutation<I, R>(options: MutationOptions<I, R>): Mutation<I>` | A write with its optimistic update, rollback and follow-up specified rather than left to each app. Runs for one `key` are serialized and different keys run at once; `optimistic` and `rollback` are transitions, passed by reference; a failure is a value in `error()`, and a cancelled run is not a failure. Unmounting aborts every request in flight and drops the queue. Legal in `*.effects.ts` only (`SHR-L004`). |
| `stream<T, M, K extends readonly unknown[]>(options: StreamOptions<T, M, K>): Stream<T>` | Push data on a reactive key. The subscription is torn down when the key changes and when the owning module unmounts; messages are folded as they arrive and the value is committed once per frame, so a flood coalesces instead of queueing. Legal in `*.effects.ts` only (`SHR-L004`). |
| `onDispose(fn: () => void): void` | Registers teardown for a subscription the runtime cannot see, such as `addEventListener` or `setInterval`. Legal in `*.effects.ts` only (SHR-L004). |
| `flush(): void` | Applies pending DOM updates now, for tests and for code that must read layout immediately after a write. |
| `html(strings: TemplateStringsArray, ...values: unknown[]): Template` | Markup with holes. A hole is reactive only when it receives the signal itself: `${total}` updates, `${total()}` is read once (SPEC §9, SHR-V003). |
| `each<T>(list: Accessor<readonly T[]> \| readonly T[], row: (item: Accessor<T>) => Template, window?: Accessor<EachWindow>): Each` | A keyed list. Objects key by `id`, primitives by value; the row function runs once per key. A `window` makes it positional instead: a fixed pool of rows, rewritten in place as the window moves, with spacers holding the rest open. |
| `render(view: () => Template, host: Element): Disposer` | Mounts `view` into `host`. It owns only the nodes it inserts, so it can live inside an app built with something else, and the disposer removes exactly those nodes. |

<!-- end generated -->

Types: `Signal<T>` (callable + `.set`), `Accessor<T>` (`() => T`), `DeepReadonly<T>`,
`Template`, `Each`, `Disposer` (a teardown that also works with `using`).

**Scheduling.** Computeds update synchronously. DOM updates wait for the next
animation frame; many writes in one frame produce one DOM write with the last
value. In unit tests call `flush()` before asserting on the DOM.

**Immutability.** Never mutate a value held in a signal. Write a new object or
array: `items.set([...items(), next])`, `items.set(items().map(o => o.id === id ? { ...o, status } : o))`.

## 3. Holes

| Value in the hole | Result |
|---|---|
| signal or computed (`${s.name}`) | reactive |
| string, number | text, escaped — never markup |
| `null`, `undefined`, `false` | nothing (attribute: removed) |
| `true` in an attribute | empty attribute (`hidden=""`) |
| `html` template | nested markup |
| a computed returning a template or `null` | conditional markup |
| `each(…)` | keyed list |

An attribute hole must be the whole value: `class=${cls}` or `class="${cls}"`.
`class="row ${x}"` throws — make `cls` a computed.

Conditional markup is a computed in the view:

```ts
const body = computed(() => {
  if (s.status() === 'loading') return html`<p data-testid="loading">Loading…</p>`;
  if (s.status() === 'error') return html`<p data-testid="error">${s.error}</p>`;
  return table;
});
return html`<main>${body}</main>`;
```

## 4. Events and intents

Views never act; they emit intents. An event hole takes a named handler —
never an inline arrow (SHR-V001). The handler receives a payload, not the Event:

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `submit` | form fields as an object; default is prevented |
| anything else | the element's `value`, or `checked` for a checkbox; `undefined` if it has neither |

The payload is read from the **element**, not chosen by the event's name, so a
component library's own event works like a native one: `@sl-change=${intent.sort}`
on an `<sl-select>` delivers its `value`. A `<button value="ascending">` names
itself the same way, which is why a `data-` attribute is never the answer.

Inside an `each` row a handler also gets a **second argument: the row's
current item** (innermost row). Every handler runs inside `batch()`.

```ts
html`<button @click=${intent.ship}>Ship</button>`   // inside a row
// effects:  ship: (_payload, order: Order) => { … }
```

## 5. Lists

`each(list, row)`: `list` is a signal/computed of an array (or a plain array,
rendered once). Objects are keyed by `id` (required, unique); primitives by
value. `row` runs **once per key** and receives an **accessor** for the item.
A new object with the same `id` updates that row's cells in place; the row is
not rebuilt. Read fields through computeds:

```ts
each(s.orders, (order) => {
  const status = computed(() => order().status);
  return html`<li data-testid="order-row">
    <span data-testid="status">${status}</span>
    <button data-testid="ship" @click=${intent.ship}>Mark shipped</button>
  </li>`;
})
```

`${order().status}` inside the row is the trap again.

**Long lists: `each(list, row, window)`.** A third argument renders only a
slice. The window is yours to measure — a `scroll` listener in `*.effects.ts`
— and `each` keeps a fixed pool of rows, rewriting their items as the window
moves instead of creating and destroying nodes:

```ts
// dashboard.effects.ts
const window = computed(() => ({
  start: Math.max(0, Math.floor(scrollTop() / ROW_HEIGHT) - OVERSCAN),
  count: VISIBLE + OVERSCAN * 2,
  rowHeight: ROW_HEIGHT,
}));

// dashboard.view.ts
each(s.rows, row, s.window)
```

The scroll container needs `overflow-anchor: none`, or the list runs away:
the spacer above the rows changes height on every step, the browser moves
`scrollTop` to hold its anchor still, and that move fires another scroll.

A windowed list is **positional, not keyed**: a slot is recycled, so a row's
node stays with the screen position rather than with its item, and `id` is not
required or checked. An out-of-range window is clamped, not an error. Use the
plain two-argument form unless the list is long enough to need this.

## 5a. Async: `resource()`, `mutation()` and `stream()`

Effects only. One primitive replaces a query library: it fetches on a reactive
key, cancels what the key replaced, retries, and keeps showing the previous
value while it revalidates.

```ts
// dashboard.effects.ts
const user = resource({
  key: () => ['user', state.userId()] as const,
  fetch: ({ key, signal }) => api.getUser(key[1], signal),
  staleAfter: 30_000,
  retry: { attempts: 3, backoff: 'exponential' },
});
```

```ts
// dashboard.view.ts — three signals, so a spinner is not woken by the value
html`${computed(() => (user.status() === 'loading' ? 'Loading…' : ''))}`
```

`status()` is `'idle' | 'loading' | 'ready' | 'error' | 'refreshing'`.
`data()` is the value for the *current* key, or `undefined`. `error()` is why
the last attempt failed. Narrow with `is()`, never by comparing `status()`:

```ts
if (user.is('ready')) user.data().name;      // data() is T here
if (user.is('error')) user.error().message;  // error() is Error here
```

What it guarantees, so you never write it again:

- The request is aborted — at the network level — when the key changes, when
  `abort()` is called, and when the module unmounts.
- A key whose contents are unchanged does not refetch, and `invalidate()`
  during a request in flight is absorbed by it.
- A response that arrives after a newer request started is discarded.
- **Cancellation is never failure:** an `AbortError` does not reach `error()`.
- `staleAfter` revalidates in the background: `'refreshing'` with `data()`
  still readable, then `'ready'`. Leave it out and a key is fetched once.
- `retry.attempts` counts the first try, so `3` is one try and two retries.
  Backoff starts at 100 ms, and `'exponential'` doubles it.

A resource holds its own value and nothing else's: there is no cache shared
between modules. Two modules asking for the same key make two requests, and
`invalidate()` on one does not touch the other.

A write is `mutation()`. `optimistic` and `rollback` are transitions from the
state module, **passed by reference** — never wrapped in an arrow, never a
direct write:

```ts
// orders.effects.ts
const ship = mutation({
  key: (order) => order.id,
  send: ({ input, signal }) => api.shipOrder(input.id, signal),
  optimistic: state.orderShipped,
  rollback: state.orderShipReverted,
  onSuccess: orders.invalidate,
});

void ship.run(order);   // resolves when this run settles; never rejects
```

- `optimistic` runs the moment `run()` is called; `send` follows.
- **Same key waits, different keys don't.** Two saves of one record are
  serialized so they cannot land in the wrong order; two different records are
  in flight at once. Leave `key` out and every run waits for the one before —
  right for a form. A key is a `string | number`, usually an id.
- A double-click is not a second write: guard with
  `if (save.status() === 'running') return;` in the effect.
- A failure calls `rollback` and lands in `error()`. A cancelled request calls
  `rollback` too — the write did not happen — but is not an error.
- An exception from `onSuccess` is reported in `error()` and rolls nothing
  back: the write already landed.
- `status()` is `'idle' | 'running' | 'done' | 'error'`. `'running'` while
  anything is in flight or queued; otherwise the outcome of the last run to
  settle, with `error()` describing that same run.
- Unmounting aborts the request in flight and drops the queue. Nothing — no
  rollback, no `onSuccess` — runs against a module that is gone, and `run()`
  after unmount does nothing.

`resource()` is request/response. Push data — a socket, an event source, a
`BroadcastChannel` — is `stream()`:

```ts
// dashboard.effects.ts
const ticks = stream({
  key: () => ['ticks', state.symbol()] as const,
  subscribe: ({ key, emit, close }) => socket.open(key[1], { onMessage: emit, onEnd: close }),
  reduce: (total, tick) => total + tick.size,   // must be O(1) per message
  initial: 0,
});
```

A stream reads like any other value — `ticks()` — with `ticks.status()`
(`'connecting' | 'open' | 'closed'`) and `ticks.error()` beside it.

- **`reduce` runs once per message; the value is written once per frame.** A
  thousand messages a second cost a thousand O(1) folds and one DOM write.
  That is why `reduce` must be O(1): an O(n) fold over a 500-row table blows
  the frame budget no matter how good the scheduler is.
- `reduceMany(previous, messages[])` is the escape hatch when per-message work
  is impossible. It is handed the whole frame's batch, and the type admits
  exactly one of the two reducers.
- `subscribe` **must return a teardown** — that is how the runtime ends the
  subscription on a key change and on unmount. It may return a promise of one,
  and the status stays `'connecting'` until it resolves.
- A new key tears down, resubscribes, and resets the value to `initial`.
- `close(reason?)` lets the adapter say the source ended. The last value stays
  readable, so a view can show it and mark it stale rather than blanking.

## 5b. Debugging: the causal trace

Development builds carry a trace of what caused what. It is off until you ask:

```js
__sheratan.start();            // in the browser console
// … reproduce the problem …
console.log(__sheratan.format());
__sheratan.stop();
```

```
write(100 → 150) @ dashboard/dashboard.effects.ts:24:7
  └─ computed #1 recomputed
      └─ computed #2 recomputed
          └─ patched <h1>
```

`__sheratan.trace()` returns the same chains as JSON —
`{ depth, dropped, entries: [{ at, cause, kind, source, from, to }] }` — which
is the form to read when the answer has to be parsed rather than eyeballed.
Steps sharing a `cause` are one chain.

Worth knowing: a write the runtime makes itself (`each` rewriting a row) is
nested under the write that caused it, not a chain of its own, and is attributed
to `sheratan`. Past 1000 writes a second the trace samples and reports how many
entries it `dropped`. None of this exists in a production build.

## 6. Module rules

The unit of code is a module: a folder under `modules/`.

```
modules/<name>/
  <name>.state.ts     signals, computeds, transitions. No I/O, no DOM.
  <name>.effects.ts   everything impure: calls to services, timers, watchers.
  <name>.view.ts      (state, intents) => html. No I/O, no writes.
  index.ts            the module's only public surface; declares its kind.
services/
  api.contract.ts     interface the modules depend on
  api.http.ts         adapter: URLs, fetch, parsing
lib/                  pure helpers, no app knowledge
ui/<component>/       stateless reusable components
app.ts                composition root: builds services, mounts modules
```

`index.ts` declares `export const kind = 'full'` (all four files) or `'view'`
(view + index only). No `shared/` folder. A component used by one module lives
inside that module.

**Import matrix** — the whole rule set for imports (SHR-L001):

| From | May import |
|---|---|
| `lib/` | `lib/`, never in a cycle |
| `ui/` | `lib/`, `ui/` |
| `services/` | `lib/`, `services/` |
| `*.state.ts` | `lib/`, own module |
| `*.effects.ts` | `lib/`, `services/` contracts, own state, other modules' `index.ts` |
| `*.view.ts` | `lib/`, `ui/`, own state |
| `index.ts` | own module files |
| `app.ts` | everything |

Any module file may also `import type` from `services/*.contract.ts` — that is
where domain types like `Customer` live — and from another module's `index.ts`,
to type a module it receives as a parameter. A value import from `services/`
in state, view or index is SHR-L001. Test files are not checked.

`sheratan` itself may be imported anywhere, but `watch` and `onDispose` belong in
effects. Data flows one way: effects → state → view.

**Transitions.** A transition is a plain function exported from the state
factory. It is the only thing that writes signals. One that writes several
signals wraps them in `batch()`. An effect that gathers several results calls
**one** transition with all of them — two calls render an in-between state.

**The state surface is read-only (SHR-L010).** `create<Name>State()` declares an
interface whose members are `Accessor` values and transitions; the `Signal`
handles stay private to `<name>.state.ts`. `Accessor<T>` is `() => T` with no
`.set`, so `state.rows.set(list)` from effects or a view does not compile.
Never type a state factory as `ReturnType<typeof create…>` — that leaks the
signals.

**State holds only what cannot be derived.** Filters, joins, counts, formatted
values and "is anything selected" are computeds, never stored.

**Cancellable I/O.** Every Promise-returning contract method takes an
`AbortSignal` (SHR-L007). Effects abort in-flight work in `onDispose`.

## 7. Canonical module

```ts
// services/api.contract.ts
export interface Customer { id: string; name: string; company: string; country: string }
export interface Api {
  listCustomers(opts: { signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<Customer[]>;
}

// services/api.http.ts
import type { Api } from './api.contract.ts';
export const createHttpApi = (base: string): Api => ({
  async listCustomers({ signal }) {
    const res = await fetch(`${base}/customers`, { signal });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error((await res.json()).error ?? `HTTP ${res.status}`);
    return res.json();
  },
});

// modules/customers/customers.state.ts
import { signal, computed, batch, type Accessor } from 'sheratan';
import type { Customer } from '../../services/api.contract.ts';

type Status = 'loading' | 'error' | 'ready';

// Declared, not inferred: accessors and transitions leave the file, signals don't (SHR-L010).
export interface CustomersState {
  readonly status: Accessor<Status>;
  readonly rows: Accessor<readonly Customer[]>;
  readonly error: Accessor<string | undefined>;
  readonly count: Accessor<number>;
  readonly loadStarted: () => void;
  readonly loaded: (list: readonly Customer[]) => void;
  readonly failed: (message: string) => void;
}

export const createCustomersState = (): CustomersState => {
  const status = signal<Status>('loading');
  const rows = signal<readonly Customer[]>([]);
  const error = signal<string | undefined>(undefined);
  return {
    status, rows, error,
    count: computed(() => rows().length),
    loadStarted: () => batch(() => { status.set('loading'); error.set(undefined); }),
    loaded: (list: readonly Customer[]) => batch(() => { rows.set(list); status.set('ready'); }),
    failed: (message: string) => batch(() => { error.set(message); status.set('error'); }),
  };
};

// modules/customers/customers.effects.ts
import { onDispose } from 'sheratan';
import type { Api } from '../../services/api.contract.ts';
import type { CustomersState } from './customers.state.ts';

export const createCustomersEffects = (api: Api, state: CustomersState) => {
  let inflight: AbortController | undefined;
  onDispose(() => inflight?.abort());
  const load = async () => {
    inflight?.abort();
    const controller = (inflight = new AbortController());
    state.loadStarted();
    try {
      state.loaded(await api.listCustomers({ signal: controller.signal }));
    } catch (err) {
      if (controller.signal.aborted) return;        // cancellation is not failure
      state.failed((err as Error).message);
    }
  };
  return { load, retry: load };
};

// modules/customers/customers.view.ts
import { html, computed, each } from 'sheratan';
import type { CustomersState } from './customers.state.ts';

export interface CustomersIntents { retry(): void }

export const customersView = (s: CustomersState, intent: CustomersIntents) => {
  const table = html`<table>
    <thead><tr><th>Name</th><th>Company</th><th>Country</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>${each(s.rows, (c) => {
      const name = computed(() => c().name);
      const company = computed(() => c().company);
      const country = computed(() => c().country);
      return html`<tr data-testid="customer-row"><td>${name}</td><td>${company}</td><td>${country}</td></tr>`;
    })}</tbody>
  </table>`;
  const body = computed(() => {
    if (s.status() === 'loading') return html`<p data-testid="loading">Loading…</p>`;
    if (s.status() === 'error') return html`<div data-testid="error">
      <p>${s.error}</p><button data-testid="retry" @click=${intent.retry}>Retry</button></div>`;
    return table;
  });
  return html`<section><h1>Customers (${s.count})</h1>${body}</section>`;
};

// modules/customers/index.ts
import type { Api } from '../../services/api.contract.ts';
import { createCustomersState } from './customers.state.ts';
import { createCustomersEffects } from './customers.effects.ts';
import { customersView } from './customers.view.ts';

export const kind = 'full';
export const createCustomers = (api: Api) => () => {
  const state = createCustomersState();
  const effects = createCustomersEffects(api, state);
  effects.load();
  return customersView(state, effects);
};

// app.ts
import { render } from 'sheratan';
import { createHttpApi } from './services/api.http.ts';
import { createCustomers } from './modules/customers/index.ts';

render(createCustomers(createHttpApi('/api')), document.getElementById('app')!);
```

Why it is shaped this way: `index.ts` returns a function, so state and effects
are created inside `render()` and everything they start is disposed with it.
The view declares the intents it needs; the effects object satisfies them.
`CustomersState` is declared rather than inferred, so effects and view hold
accessors and cannot write a signal even by accident.

## 8. Tests

State is pure and needs no mocks. Effects get a fake `Api` object.

```ts
const s = createCustomersState();
s.loaded([{ id: '1', name: 'Ada', company: 'X', country: 'UK' }]);
assert.equal(s.count(), 1);
assert.equal(s.status(), 'ready');
```

Tests are `<name>.state.test.ts` and `<name>.effects.test.ts` next to the
module (SHR-T001 warns when missing). End-to-end tests live in `e2e/`.

## 9. Wrong → right

| Wrong | Right | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `${s.total()}` in a hole | `${s.total}` | V003 |
| `${a() + b()}` in a hole | `const sum = computed(() => a() + b())`, then `${sum}` | V003 |
| `@click=${() => intent.ship(id)}` | `@click=${intent.ship}` inside the row; handler reads its 2nd argument | V001 |
| `fetch(…)` in a view or state | contract method in `services/`, called from effects | L002 / L001 |
| `state.rows.set(list)` in effects | a transition: `state.loaded(list)` | L005 |
| state exposes `rows: Signal<T>` | `rows: Accessor<T>` plus a transition that writes it | L010 |
| `import { x } from '../orders/orders.state.ts'` | `import { … } from '../orders/index.ts'` (effects only) | L001 |
| view imports effects | the view receives intents as a parameter | L001 |
| `state.a(x); state.b(y);` after one await | one transition taking `{ x, y }` | — |
| storing a filtered list in a signal | `computed(() => rows().filter(…))` | — |
| `order().status` read directly in a row hole | `computed(() => order().status)` | V003 |
| `listCustomers(): Promise<…>` without a signal | `listCustomers(opts: { signal: AbortSignal })` | L007 |
| `items().push(x)` | `items.set([...items(), x])` | L011 |
| `watch`/`onDispose` in a view | move to effects | L004 |

## 10. Checker output

`sheratan check --json` prints one object per violation:

```json
{
  "code": "SHR-L001",
  "severity": "error",
  "file": "modules/todo/todo.view.ts",
  "range": { "line": 3, "column": 1 },
  "message": "view cannot import effects; allowed: lib, ui, own state.",
  "fix": "Move the call into todo.effects.ts and expose the result via todo.state.ts.",
  "docs": "https://sheratan.dev/errors/SHR-L001"
}
```

Apply the `fix`; the `message` names the allowed set.

| Code | Rule |
|---|---|
| SHR-L001 | import not allowed by the matrix, including deep imports past another module's `index.ts` |
| SHR-L002 | I/O global (`fetch`, `localStorage`, `document`, timers) in a view or state |
| SHR-L003 | `shared/` folder at any depth, or a file under `ui/` outside a component folder (loose in `ui/`, or nested below the component) |
| SHR-L004 | `watch`, `onDispose`, `resource`, `mutation`, `stream` (and later `navigate`) outside effects |
| SHR-L005 | effects write a signal directly instead of calling a transition |
| SHR-L006 | module files don't match its declared `kind` |
| SHR-L007 | Promise-returning contract method without an `AbortSignal` |
| SHR-L008 | circular imports between modules, or among `lib/` files |
| SHR-L009 | module stylesheet not wrapped in its `@scope` |
| SHR-L010 | a `*.state.ts` exposes a `Signal`; only accessors and transitions leave the file |
| SHR-L011 | mutating a value read from a signal (`items().push(x)`) instead of `.set()` |
| SHR-V001 | inline function in a template hole (error) |
| SHR-V002 | `unsafeHTML` with a non-literal argument (warning) |
| SHR-V003 | signal called inside a hole (warning) |
| SHR-V004 | malformed template (error) |
| SHR-T001 | module has no state/effects tests (warning) |

## Not in v0

`mount()`, `unsafeHTML` and routing are specified but not shipped.
